questionText:
Geetha has a conjecture about integers, which is of the form

$$\forall x \left( P(x) \implies \exists y Q(x, y) \right),$$

where $P$ is a statement about integers, and $Q$ is a statement about pairs of integers. Which of the following (one or more) option(s) would imply Geetha's conjecture?
explanation:
Conjecture: $G = \forall x \left( P(x) \implies \exists y Q(x, y) \right)$

Analysis of Options:
• (B) $\forall x \forall y Q(x, y)$: If $Q(x, y)$ is true for all $x, y$, then $\exists y Q(x,y)$ is always true. Thus, $P(x) \implies \exists y Q(x, y)$ holds universally for all $x$, implying $G$.
• (C) $\exists y \forall x \left( P(x) \implies Q(x, y) \right)$: Selecting a fixed $y_0$ for which $P(x) \implies Q(x, y_0)$ holds for every $x$ directly ensures that for every $x$, there exists at least one $y$ (namely $y_0$) satisfying $Q(x, y)$. Hence, (C) implies $G$.
